summary: Ghanzi Airport (GNZ) is a small regional airport serving the town of Ghanzi in western Botswana, the administrative capital of the Ghanzi District. The airport primarily handles light aircraft and charter flights, serving as an important access point for travelers heading to the Central Kalahari Game Reserve and surrounding cattle-ranching communities. It plays a vital role in connecting this remote area to Botswana's capital, Gaborone, and other regional destinations.
faqs:
Q: Where is Ghanzi Airport located?
A: Ghanzi Airport is located near the town of Ghanzi in western Botswana, approximately 3 km from the town center along the Trans-Kalahari Highway.

Q: What type of aircraft use Ghanzi Airport?
A: The airport primarily accommodates small turboprop aircraft and private planes, as it has a relatively short unpaved or semi-paved runway suited for light aviation.

Q: Are there commercial flights to Ghanzi Airport?
A: Scheduled commercial service is very limited. Most visitors fly via charter or private aircraft, while some may use scheduled services when available.

Q: What is the best time to visit the Ghanzi region?
A: The cooler dry season from May to September is ideal, offering pleasant temperatures and excellent wildlife viewing in the nearby Central Kalahari Game Reserve.
transport_tips: Taxis and pre-arranged transfers are the most common ways to reach Ghanzi town from the airport, as public transport options are limited in this remote area. Renting a 4x4 vehicle is highly recommended if you plan to explore the Central Kalahari Game Reserve or surrounding areas. Road conditions on the Trans-Kalahari Highway are generally good, but gravel roads in the region require a sturdy vehicle.
local_tip: If you're visiting for the famous Ghanzi Bushman Cultural Festival or heading into the Central Kalahari Game Reserve, coordinate your ground transport well in advance, as services are sparse and bookings fill up quickly during peak tourist season.
